rationale:
Evidence: the only race data is iteration 0 (kp 4, ki 0.1, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.8, weights -2..2, 12 mm sensors at y 0.05). All 60 trials ended off-track on oval, s-bend and slalom, with progress only 0.13 to 0.20. Steering oscillation was 0.11 to 0.16, and line-loss events occurred in 1 to 2 runs per track. Max error sat at the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the robot diverged rather than wandering. Iteration 1 was never raced, so there is no new evidence on it.

Diagnosis: with weights spanning -2..2 across the 0.048 m sensor row, the signal is roughly the lateral offset in units of 12 mm. At kp 4 a 12 mm offset gives turn about 4, which is about 1400 PWM of wheel differential. That is too much for the lag between the sensors (0.05 m ahead of the axle) and the motors at 1.8 base speed. Each correction overshoots and the oscillation grows until the tape is lost. Derivative action was too weak to damp it.

Changes: (1) kp 4.0 to 2.0, halving the steering gain so corrections are smaller and less overshoot. (2) kd 0.5 to 1.2, adding damping against the fast signal changes that drive the oscillation. (3) ki 0.1 to 0.0, because the drift is oscillatory, not a steady offset, and integral action only adds windup on bends. (4) base_speed 1.8 to 1.3, giving the controller time to correct on the bends. Off-track ends are worth far more than the speed term, so I accept that completion inside 3 s may be lost. (5) Geometry is kept: five sensors at 12 mm spacing keep at least two on the 25 mm tape, and the sensor lead at y 0.05 is kept for anticipation. Weights and line_loss (last_direction) stay the same.

Expected result: much lower oscillation and fewer off-track ends. I expect progress well above 0.2, possibly completing the oval. Completion time may be 3.2 s or more, so the speed term may be small. Main risk: kp 2.0 may be too weak for the sharpest slalom bends, so the next round should check the slalom progress first.
